name: admin.analytics.getFile
summary: Retrieve analytics data for a given date, presented as a compressed JSON file

args.name: token
args.description: Authentication token bearing required scopes. Tokens should be passed as an HTTP Authorization header or alternatively, as a POST parameter.

args.name: type
args.description: The type of analytics to retrieve. The options are currently limited to `member` (for Enterprise org member analytics) and `public_channel` (for public channel analytics).

args.name: date
args.description: Date to retrieve the analytics data for, expressed as `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC. Required unless `metadata_only` is set to true.

args.name: metadata_only
args.description: Retrieve metadata for the `type` of analytics indicated. Can be used only with `type` set to `public_channel` analytics. See [detail below](#metadata_only). Omit the `date` parameter when using this argument.

name: admin.analytics.messages.activity
summary: Retrieves activity metrics for messages from a given channel.

args.name: channel
args.description: Channel ID for channel of the message activity to query.

args.name: oldest_ts
args.description: Oldest timestamp to include in the results. Defaults to 7 days before current time. If not passed while still passing the `latest_ts` parameter, defaults to 7 days before `latest_ts`.

args.name: latest_ts
args.description: Most recent timestamp to include in results. Defaults to current time. If not passed while still passing the `oldest_ts` parameter, defaults to 7 days after `oldest_ts`.

args.name: cursor
args.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the `cursor` parameter to a `next_cursor` attribute returned by a previous request's `response_metadata`. Default value fetches the first "page" of the collection.

args.name: limit
args.description: Maximum number of entries to return. Defaults to 50 if not passed. Max allowed is 100.

name: admin.apps.activities.list
summary: Get logs for a specified team/org

args.name: token
args.description: Authentication token bearing required scopes. Tokens should be passed as an HTTP Authorization header or alternatively, as a POST parameter.

args.name: app_id
args.description: The ID of the app to get activities from.

args.name: team_id
args.description: The team who owns this log.

args.name: cursor
args.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the `cursor` parameter to a `next_cursor` attribute returned by a previous request's `response_metadata`. See [pagination](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/pagination.md) for more detail.

args.name: limit
args.description: The maximum number of items to return.

args.name: min_log_level
args.description: The minimum log level of the log events to be returned. Defaults to `info`. Acceptable values (in order of relative importance from smallest to largest) are `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` and `fatal`.

args.name: log_event_type
args.description: The event type of log events to be returned.

args.name: source
args.description: The source of log events to be returned. Acceptable values are `slack` and `developer`.

args.name: component_type
args.description: The component type of log events to be returned. Acceptable values are `events_api`, `workflows`, `functions` and `tables`.

args.name: component_id
args.description: The component ID of log events to be returned. Will be `FnXXXXXX` for functions, and `WfXXXXXX` for workflows

args.name: trace_id
args.description: The trace ID of log events to be returned.

args.name: min_date_created
args.description: The earliest timestamp of the log to retrieve (epoch microseconds).

args.name: max_date_created
args.description: The latest timestamp of the log to retrieve (epoch microseconds).

args.name: sort_direction
args.description: The direction you want the data sorted by (always by timestamp) _Acceptable values:_ `asc` `desc`

args.description: Set `cursor` to `next_cursor` returned by the previous call to list items in the next page

args.description: The number of results that will be returned by the API on each invocation

args.description: Only include workflows with no collaborators in the result; default is false

args.name: collaborator_ids
args.description: Only include workflows where all of the provided user IDs are a manager/collaborator of that workflow

args.name: num_trigger_ids
args.description: Number of trigger IDs to fetch for each workflow; default is 10

args.name: is_sales_elevate
args.description: Filter workflows by their Sales Elevate status

args.name: source
args.description: Source of workflow creation, either from code or workflow builder _Acceptable values:_ `code` `workflow_builder` `sales_home` `agent`

args.name: sort
args.description: The field used to sort the returned workflows _Acceptable values:_ `name`

args.name: sort_dir
args.description: Sort direction. Possible values are `asc` for ascending order like (1, 2, 3) or (a, b, c), and `desc` for descending order like (3, 2, 1) or (c, b, a) _Acceptable values:_ `asc` `desc`

args.name: trigger_type_id
args.description: Only include workflows with this trigger type

args.name: publish_status
args.description: Filter workflows by their published status _Acceptable values:_ `all` `published` `unpublished`

args.name: step_function_ids
args.description: Only include workflows that use all of the provided step function ids

name: agents.conversations.create
summary: Creates a dedicated code channel for an agent session.

args.name: token
args.description: Authentication token bearing the `code_channels:manage` scope. Must be a granular bot token.

args.name: name
args.description: A friendly display name for the code channel. Optional when `origin_channel_id` and `origin_message_ts` are provided — in that case the channel is named from the origin message and re-titled automatically. Required when no origin link is given.

args.name: team_id
args.description: Encoded team id to create the channel in. Required for org tokens when `origin_channel_id` is not provided. When omitted, the workspace is derived from the origin channel.

args.name: session_id
args.description: An opaque identifier for the agent session. When provided, the call is idempotent: if a channel already exists for this `session_id`, it is returned instead of creating a new one.

args.name: is_private
args.description: Whether the code channel is private. When omitted, the channel matches the privacy of `origin_channel_id`, or is public if no origin is given. An explicit value is always honored, even if it differs from the origin channel's privacy: passing `false` creates a public channel from a private origin.

args.name: origin_channel_id
args.description: The channel ID where the agent session was initiated from. Must be provided together with `origin_message_ts`. The channel must be accessible to the calling user and must not be externally shared (Slack Connect). When `team_id` is omitted with an org token, the channel is created in the same workspace as this origin channel.

args.name: origin_message_ts
args.description: The message timestamp in the origin channel that started the agent session. Must be provided together with `origin_channel_id`. The author of this message is automatically invited to the newly created code channel.

name: agents.conversations.setView
summary: Creates or updates a view in a code channel. Views can render HTML, diffs, Block Kit, or canvases as tabs alongside the conversation.

args.name: token
args.description: Authentication token bearing the `code_channels:manage` scope. Must be a granular bot token.

args.name: channel_id
args.description: ID of the code channel to render the view in.

args.name: type
args.description: The kind of view to create or update. Defaults to `html`. Determines which other arguments are required: `html` and `diff` require `content`, `block_kit` requires `blocks`, and `canvas` requires `canvas_id`.

args.name: view_key
args.description: Agent-assigned stable identity for the view (e.g. the source file path on the agent's machine). Used as the upsert key: calls with the same `view_key` update the same view. Required for `html`, `block_kit`, and `canvas` views; ignored for `diff` (a `diff` view is a per-channel singleton).

args.name: content
args.description: View content. For `html`, a full self-contained HTML document; for `diff`, raw unified diff text. Capped at 1,000,000 bytes; larger content returns `content_too_large`. The cap is enforced by the handler (not schema `maxLength`) so the documented error code actually surfaces instead of a generic argument-validation failure. Required when `type` is `html` or `diff`.

args.name: blocks
args.description: Block Kit blocks to render in the view tab. Required when `type` is `block_kit`; ignored otherwise.

args.name: canvas_id
args.description: Encoded ID of the canvas to attach as the view. Required when `type` is `canvas`; ignored otherwise.

args.name: access_level
args.description: For `canvas` views: access level granted to the channel for the canvas tab. Defaults to `write`. Use `comment` to grant channel members comment access (read and comment, no editing) so the agent remains the sole author of the canvas text. _Acceptable values:_ `read` `write` `comment`

args.name: agent_content_hash
args.description: For `canvas` views: hash of the canvas-derived markdown the agent last wrote, recorded so the agent can later detect human edits to the canvas. Opaque to the server.

args.name: base_branch
args.description: For `diff` views: base branch name for display purposes.

args.name: head_branch
args.description: For `diff` views: head branch name for display purposes.

args.name: name
args.description: Display label for the view tab. Preferred over the legacy `label` argument (`name` wins if both are supplied). Defaults to the last path segment of `view_key`, stripped of any `.html` or `.htm` extension.

args.name: label
args.description: Deprecated alias for `name`. Display label for the view tab. Defaults to the last path segment of `view_key`, stripped of any `.html` or `.htm` extension.

args.name: csp
args.description: Content-Security-Policy domain declarations for the view. Domains are validated server-side (`https://` only, no private or internal hosts) and persisted.

args.name: token
args.description: Authentication token bearing required scopes. Tokens should be passed as an HTTP Authorization header or alternatively, as a POST parameter.

args.name: channel
args.description: Channel ID of the message. Both `channel` and `ts` must be provided together, _or_ `unfurl_id` and `source` must be provided together. Required for public channels.

args.description: Timestamp of the message to add unfurl behavior to. Required for public channels.

args.description: Set to `true` or `1` to indicate the user must install your Slack app to trigger unfurls for this domain

args.name: user_auth_url

args.name: user_auth_blocks

args.name: unfurl_id

args.name: source
args.description: The source of the link to unfurl. The source may either be `composer`, when the link is inside the message composer, or `conversations_history`, when the link has been posted to a conversation. _Acceptable values:_ `composer` `conversations_history`

name: chat.update
summary: Updates a message.

args.name: token
args.description: Authentication token bearing required scopes. Tokens should be passed as an HTTP Authorization header or alternatively, as a POST parameter.

args.name: channel
args.description: Channel containing the message to be updated. For direct messages, ensure that this value is a DM ID (starts with `D`) instead of a User ID (starts with either `U` or `W`).

args.name: ts
args.description: Timestamp of the message to be updated.

args.name: as_user
args.description: Pass true to update the message as the authed user. Bot users in this context are considered authed users.

args.name: attachments
args.description: A JSON-based array of structured attachments, presented as a URL-encoded string.

args.name: unfurled_attachments
args.description: A JSON-based array of structured attachments, presented as a URL-encoded string.

args.name: blocks
args.description: A JSON-based array of structured blocks, presented as a URL-encoded string.

args.name: markdown_text
args.description: Accepts message text formatted in markdown. This argument should not be used in conjunction with `blocks` or `text`. Limit this field to 12,000 characters.

args.name: metadata
args.description: JSON object with event\_type and event\_payload fields, presented as a URL-encoded string. If you don't include this field, the message's previous `metadata` will be retained. To remove previous `metadata`, include an empty object for this field. Metadata you post to Slack is accessible to any app or user who is a member of that workspace.

args.name: link_names
args.description: Find and link channel names and usernames. Defaults to `none`. If you do not specify a value for this field, the original value set for the message will be overwritten with the default, `none`.

args.name: parse
args.description: Change how messages are treated. Defaults to `client`, unlike `chat.postMessage`. Accepts either `none` or `full`. If you do not specify a value for this field, the original value set for the message will be overwritten with the default, `client`.

args.name: text

args.name: reply_broadcast
args.description: Broadcast an existing thread reply to make it visible to everyone in the channel or conversation.

args.name: file_ids
args.description: Array of new file ids that will be sent with this message.

args.name: include_archived
args.description: Must match the `include_archived` passed to `slackLists.download.start`. The returned `download_url` carries this through so the served export includes archived items when they were requested.
